explanation: I found no Mathlib declaration that states this result. The theorem is about `IsGradedExtInternallyFinite`, a predicate the library defines itself. It says the predicate is preserved when the source object is replaced by `e.inverse.obj X`. Its proof is a one-line wrapper that applies the library's own lemma `gradedExtShiftSourceInverse` to the `finiteLaurentSupport` field. Mathlib has no notion of internally finite graded Ext with respect to an autoequivalence, and nothing about Laurent support of graded Ext groups. So the content of the theorem lies entirely in the library's definitions. Because the statement is built on library-only notions, I did not run a separate search of Mathlib.
